intro: Wednesday June 25 — for the June 26 session. REGIME UPDATE: the strongest single-night AI fundamental session of the 2026 cycle has arrived. Micron delivered $41.5B Q3 (vs. $34.66B consensus) + $50B Q4 guidance, simultaneously with Qualcomm unveiling Dragonfly (C1000 CPU + AI300 inference accelerator) with Meta as anchor customer and $15B data center revenue by 2029. MU +16%, QCOM +12%, SK Hynix +11.1%, KOSPI +5.42%, NQ futures +2.1%. WTI $69.42/bbl (below $70 for the first time since 2024), Brent $73.05 (-5.2%), Gold $3,987 (-3.07%). Macro gates on June 25: VIX premarket 18.32 (above 17 — gate still breached, tightening), DXY 101.27 (above 100 — gate still breached, tightening), SPX regime assessment pending PCE. CRITICAL: May PCE at 8:30 AM ET (12:30 UTC) and Q1 GDP Third Estimate are the final macro gates for the June 25 session. WTI $69.42 / Brent $73.05 (-5.2%) are powerful disinflation inputs that increase cold PCE probability (core below 3.2%). Cold PCE = VIX compression below 17, DXY below 100, regime gates cleared — HIGH conviction across the board. BTC EXCEPTION: BTC is NOT participating in the strongest AI equity session of 2026 (BTC +0.4% vs NQ +2.1%) — this non-participation in the best fundamental AI catalyst of the cycle is the dominant structural bear signal for crypto. Do not interpret the AI equity risk-on as a BTC re-entry signal. Framework: cold PCE clears macro gates for NVDA/MU/SK HYNIX; BTC gate is separate (two consecutive UTC closes above $62,000 required; not yet achieved).

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: DUAL AI DEMAND CONFIRMATION — Micron $50B Q4 + Qualcomm Dragonfly simultaneously validated the full AI infrastructure stack. NVDA premarket est. ~$207–$210 on dual read-through. Add on cold PCE (8:30 AM ET) at $205–$209 open. Stop $195 daily close.
ideas.why: June 24 AH + June 25 premarket delivered the dual AI demand confirmation the framework required: (1) Micron Q3 $41.5B (vs. $34.66B consensus) + Q4 $50B guide — HBM4 sold-out through 2026-2027 directly validates NVDA's Vera Rubin memory supply chain; (2) Qualcomm Dragonfly data center debut (C1000 CPU + AI300 inference accelerator, Meta as anchor customer) confirms AI data center spend is expanding from GPU to full-stack silicon — every hyperscaler that buys Qualcomm Dragonfly servers also buys NVDA H200/H300/Vera Rubin GPUs for training. The compound signal is the most bullish NVDA configuration since the B100 launch: simultaneous memory supply chain confirmation (MU +16%) + inference stack validation (QCOM +12%) + hyperscaler anchor (Meta) = AI capex cycle intact, NVDA remains the apex beneficiary. Macro gate caveat: VIX 18.32 / DXY 101.27 premarket — cold PCE (12:30 UTC) clears both gates; hot PCE resets the framework. Add is conditional on PCE.
ideas.trigger: June 25 PCE cold (core below 3.2%): add NVDA at $205–$209 on the open or first pullback after PCE. June 25 PCE in-line (core 3.2–3.4%): hold existing position, add only on confirmed SPX close above 7,460. June 25 PCE hot (core above 3.5%): do not add; reduce half position if held; re-enter on confirmed regime gate clearance. Stop: $195 daily close. Catalyst: Qualcomm Dragonfly customer adoption news (Meta production deployment date) + NVDA Q2 pre-announcement window (late July).
ideas.risk: PCE hot (core above 3.5%) — 30Y tests 5.00%, DXY above 102, VIX spikes above 20; AI multiple compression overrides both Micron and Qualcomm catalysts; hyperscalers signal Qualcomm Dragonfly reduces GPU dependency rather than coexisting with NVDA; NVDA management issues cautious supply chain commentary before Q2 earnings.

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.idea: BEAT-AND-RAISE CONFIRMED — $41.5B Q3 (vs. $34.66B consensus) + $50B Q4 guide. MU +16% premarket. Add on cold PCE at the $1,200–$1,250 open range. HBM4 sold out through 2026-2027 is the structural buy signal for the next two quarters.
ideas.why: Micron delivered the most significant beat-and-raise in the AI semiconductor cycle: $41.5B Q3 revenue (vs. $34.66B consensus, a $6.84B / 19.7% beat) + $50B Q4 guidance ($14B above the prior consensus of ~$36B). The $50B Q4 guide is not incremental — it is a structural re-rating event confirming: (1) HBM4 sold-out through 2026-2027 with pricing power; (2) NVIDIA Vera Rubin qualification is de-risked; (3) the enterprise AI memory transition (DDR5 → HBM4) is accelerating faster than sell-side models projected. MU +16% premarket reflects the 2.9-sigma positive surprise across all three metrics (revenue, EPS, gross margin). The risk-reward for adding at the $1,200–$1,250 open: MU's buy-side consensus target is $1,450+ post-guidance revision. Stop at $990 two-close basis. The conviction upgrade from MEDIUM (pre-print) to HIGH is direct.
ideas.trigger: Add at $1,200–$1,250 range on June 26 open after cold PCE confirmation (8:30 AM ET June 25). If MU gaps above $1,300: wait for first-hour pullback to $1,250–$1,270 before adding. Cold PCE required — if PCE hot, do not add; hold existing. Stop: $990 two-close basis. Target: $1,400+ on sustained HBM4 pricing power confirmation.
ideas.risk: Hot PCE June 25 → risk-off overrides the beat; Samsung announces confirmed NVIDIA HBM4E qualification on the same timeline as MU's sold-out claim — market share re-rating; Micron confirms capacity expansion exceeding HBM4 supply constraint (pricing power thesis broken); enterprise AI budget freeze signals in hyperscaler commentary July.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: UPGRADED TO HIGH CONVICTION — ₩2,917,000 June 25 KST close (+11.1%), ₩2,000 from ATH close reclaim. Micron $50B Q4 guide directly validates 58% HBM market share thesis. Dual read-through from both Micron (direct) and Qualcomm Dragonfly (inference stack adoption) confirms AI memory demand is structural.
ideas.why: SK Hynix June 25 KST session: +11.1%, KOSPI +5.42% to 8,930.30. The ₩2,917,000 close is ₩377,000 above the ₩2,540,000 framework stop — the most comfortable stop buffer since the KOSPI Black Tuesday panic. Two simultaneous validation signals: (1) Micron's $50B Q4 HBM4 guide directly confirms SK Hynix's 58% HBM market share is structural — if MU Q4 is $50B, SK Hynix's July 29 Q2 earnings will show commensurate HBM4 revenue growth; (2) Qualcomm Dragonfly (AI300 inference accelerator) uses HBM memory — Qualcomm's data center push creates a second memory demand channel beyond GPU training. Framework stop ₩2,540,000 remains live but at ₩377,000 buffer — the highest-conviction add window since the ADR SEC clearance and July 29 earnings catalysts remain ahead. The June 23 HBM4 capacity slowdown report (Korean media) is structurally refuted by Micron's $50B Q4 guidance — a competitor cannot guide to $50B Q4 AI memory revenue if HBM4 capacity is actually being slowed.
ideas.trigger: Hold core long through June 26 KST open. If KST session consolidates at ₩2,800,000–₩2,950,000: add on the first pullback. Add condition: cold PCE June 25 clears macro gates (VIX below 17, DXY below 100). Stop: ₩2,540,000 (two consecutive KST daily closes below required for full exit — framework unchanged). ADR SEC clearance announcement is a secondary non-PCE-dependent catalyst. Target: ATH close reclaim at ₩2,919,000 then ₩3,000,000+.
ideas.risk: Hot PCE June 25 reverses KOSPI risk-on sentiment; Samsung announces NVIDIA HBM4E qualification — direct SK Hynix market share threat; Korea geopolitical escalation (North Korea missile test into a risk-on session amplifies any reversal); SK Hynix management officially confirms HBM4 capacity slowdown at any forum before July 29 Q2 earnings.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: NON-PARTICIPATION IS THE DOMINANT SIGNAL — BTC +0.4% while NQ +2.1%, MU +16%, SK Hynix +11.1%. The best AI fundamental session of the 2026 cycle drove zero BTC participation. Do NOT re-enter until two consecutive UTC closes above $62,000. June 25 session high $61,967 — $33 below the gate.
ideas.why: The structural breakdown thesis from the June 24 UTC stop execution ($61,078.01 close, below $62,000) is strengthened by June 25's non-participation: BTC +0.25–0.40% (Crypto.com live $61,325.96 at 11:01 UTC) while the strongest AI fundamental session of the 2026 cycle drove NQ +2.1%, MU +16%, QCOM +12%, SK Hynix +11.1%. The June 25 session high of $61,967 is $33 below the $62,000 re-entry gate. If BTC cannot clear $62,000 on this fundamental environment, distribution is occurring at scale. The framework is unchanged: do NOT re-enter on equity risk-on bids. PCE at 12:30 UTC is the within-session catalyst — cold PCE could spike BTC toward $62,000–$63,000, which would constitute Day 1 of the re-entry clock at the 20:00 UTC close. Conviction downgraded from HIGH to MEDIUM because the $59,105 post-stop low has held for 36+ hours and the $61,967 session high is the closest BTC has been to the gate since stop execution.
ideas.trigger: REMAIN FLAT. Watch June 25 UTC close at 20:00 UTC (4 PM ET) — must close ABOVE $62,000 for Day 1. Cold PCE (12:30 UTC) is the potential catalyst for a spike through $62,000. If BTC closes above $62,000 June 25: Day 1 activated; watch June 26 UTC close. Two consecutive closes above $62,000 required before any re-entry. Do NOT buy intraday spikes above $62,000 — only closes count. If June 25 closes below $62,000: remain flat; earliest re-entry clock June 26 at earliest.
ideas.risk: Cold PCE spikes BTC through $62,000 at 12:30 UTC and the 20:00 UTC daily close confirms above $62,000 — Day 1 activated; if June 26 also closes above $62,000, re-entry framework activates and MEDIUM conviction becomes HIGH for the long side; IBIT institutional inflows resume at scale before PCE — the institutional bid changes the structural narrative.

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: QUALCOMM DRAGONFLY ANCHOR CUSTOMER — Meta is the first disclosed Qualcomm Dragonfly customer (C1000 CPU + AI300 inference accelerator); this is not incidental AI capex validation, it is Meta's inference infrastructure thesis confirmed by a competing silicon supplier at commercial scale.
ideas.why: Meta as Qualcomm Dragonfly anchor customer is a three-layer validation for META stock: (1) Meta's inference infrastructure is real, commercial, and scaling NOW — not in 2027; (2) Meta is buying best-in-class inference accelerators (AI300) separately from GPU training, indicating it is building a multi-vendor AI silicon stack that reduces risk concentration and increases total AI spend; (3) the $15B Qualcomm data center revenue by 2029 target means Meta alone is committing significant inference capex on Qualcomm silicon, confirming META's AI monetization flywheel is operational. The near-term catalyst: cold PCE at 8:30 AM ET clears the VIX/DXY gates that have prevented the META upgrade from WATCH to BUY. Meta fundamental metrics remain the strongest in Mag-7: lowest forward P/E post-FOMC selloff, self-funded AI build (no external financing needed), advertising revenue directly monetizing AI inference capacity. Add on cold PCE at $540–$560.
ideas.trigger: June 25 cold PCE (core below 3.2%): add META at $540–$560 market. If META gaps above $570 on cold PCE: wait for first-hour pullback. In-line PCE (core 3.2–3.4%): hold existing; do not add. Hot PCE: do not add; hold existing with $520 stop. Catalyst accelerator: Qualcomm partnership announcement expansion or Meta-specific inference deployment disclosure. Stop: $520 daily close.
ideas.risk: PCE hot overrides the Qualcomm validation; regulatory risk (EU Digital Markets Act enforcement action timing); Qualcomm Dragonfly inference advantage proves inferior to NVIDIA alternative (H100/H200 inference efficiency) causing a reversal of the narrative; Meta advertising revenue deceleration in Q2 earnings (late July) contradicts the AI monetization thesis.

ideas.name: Qualcomm
ideas.idea: DRAGONFLY DATA CENTER DEBUT — first non-NVIDIA commercial AI data center silicon with a named hyperscaler anchor (Meta). $15B data center revenue target by 2029. QCOM +12% premarket. Add on PCE-driven pullback; do not chase the gap.
ideas.why: Qualcomm's Dragonfly platform (C1000 data center CPU + AI300 inference accelerator) with Meta as anchor customer is the most significant non-NVIDIA AI data center silicon launch since AMD's MI300X deployment. The investment thesis: (1) Qualcomm captures inference workloads that currently default to NVIDIA because no credible alternative exists — the AI300 changes that calculus; (2) $15B data center revenue by 2029 represents a new vertical for a company that was exclusively mobile/auto/IoT — this is a total addressable market expansion, not a product refresh; (3) Meta as anchor customer provides commercial validation that the inference economics are superior enough to justify switching from the existing NVIDIA-dominated stack. The conviction is MEDIUM (not HIGH) because: (a) Dragonfly is brand new — volume production and delivery timelines are unconfirmed; (b) QCOM +12% premarket has already priced much of the near-term upside; (c) PCE is the session macro gate. Add on PCE-driven pullback, not the open gap.
ideas.trigger: Add on first PCE-driven pullback from the gap — target $195–$205 entry on cold PCE (below the $210–$215 gap open estimate). If QCOM consolidates above $200 on above-average volume for two sessions: add second tranche. Hot PCE: do not add; wait for pullback to $185. Stop: $175 daily close. Target: $225+ on Dragonfly volume production confirmation and second named customer.
ideas.risk: Dragonfly volume production delays push commercial availability beyond H2 2026; NVIDIA announces competing inference accelerator platform within 30 days; Meta reduces Dragonfly allocation after initial deployment test (not a full production commitment); PCE hot drives broad tech multiple compression overriding the structural Dragonfly thesis.

ideas.name: Alphabet
ideas.idea: Watch only — Qualcomm Dragonfly (Meta anchor) raises the question of whether Google's TPU inference strategy is competitively superior or merely parallel to the Qualcomm approach; Google Cloud AI inference is the differentiated asset; PCE + VIX/DXY gates must clear before adding.
ideas.why: Alphabet's investment case for the June 26 session rests on a three-part read: (1) Qualcomm Dragonfly with Meta as anchor customer validates enterprise AI inference at commercial scale — Google Cloud's TPU v6 inference offering is a direct competitor; if Meta is buying from Qualcomm AND Google Cloud, that is a demand expansion thesis; if Meta's Qualcomm purchase is a Google Cloud alternative, that is a competitive risk; (2) NVDA Vera Rubin supply chain confirmation (via Micron $50B Q4) benefits Google's training infrastructure investments; (3) Google's advertising revenue is the closest structural analog to Meta's Qualcomm anchor story. The WATCH designation reflects: all three macro gates still partially breached premarket (VIX 18.32 above 17 gate); GOOGL has the highest regulatory uncertainty in Mag-7 (DOJ antitrust ongoing); and the Qualcomm/Meta relationship requires 2–3 days of analyst clarification before GOOGL's competitive positioning is definitive. Cold PCE clearing VIX/DXY gates would upgrade GOOGL to LOW-MEDIUM buy.
ideas.trigger: Watch through June 25 PCE. Cold PCE + VIX below 17 + DXY below 100: upgrade to medium conviction, add GOOGL at $175–$185. Monitor Qualcomm Dragonfly analyst notes for competitive positioning vs Google TPU. Stop on any existing position: $165 daily close. Priority: NVDA and MU are higher-conviction additions first; add GOOGL only after primary AI-semi positions are sized.
ideas.risk: Qualcomm Dragonfly proves to be a direct alternative to Google Cloud TPU inference — Google Cloud loses Meta as a primary inference customer; DOJ antitrust ruling triggers forced Google ad business restructuring; PCE hot drives tech multiple compression before the Qualcomm/Google competitive picture clears.
